evidence.excerpt:
Only Look Once version 11 
was used as a fixed detector and trained under identical conditions at 640 × 640 resolution 
for 100 epochs. Performance was evaluated primarily using mean average precision over 
intersection-over-union thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95, supported by mean average precision 
at 0.50, precision, recall, and F1 -score. Size-ordered splitting reduced the primary metric to 
0.124 in Dataset 1 and as low as 0.005 in Dataset 2, whereas size -aware stratification 
recovered competitive values of 0.523 and 0.477, respectively. These findings indicate that 
dataset partitioning is a consequential data -level design factor and can support more 
dependable benchmarking for automated license -plate recognition, intelligent 
transportation, traffic monitoring, and surveillance applications. 
 
Keywords:

Object size is considered in this study as a determinant in the ability to influence the learning and assessment results of detectors. 
Instead of considering the traditional split as necessarily representative, we check the possibility that the object -size spectrum 
can irregularly cluster in the training, validation and test sets, and thus estimate performance biasedly. To define realisti c cases 
and controlled remedies, four partitioning scenarios are characterized, the first three represent an unsorted nat ural split, a 
descending size-ordered split, and a size -descending stratified split, whereas the fourth applies purposeful size -aware stratified 
sampling. After each partition is generated, its representativeness is assessed using KL divergence and normalized Earth Mover's 
Distance (EMD) before model training and performance evaluation.

selected randomly, and 70 percent of the sample is selected as the training samples, 20 percent of the sample is selected as the 
validation samples, and 10 percent of the sample is selected as the test set rather than further quantizing each category into bins. 
The summation of the subsets in the three categories sampled results in final splits. The method is a tradeoff between extrem ely 
quantized stratification by maintaining a coarse degree of balance between the sizes of items with each other, and total random 
assignment. 
 Summary of Partitioning Scenarios 
The four situations collectively represent a wide range of database organization techniques:  
● Scenarios 1: Natural unsorted sequential splitting without reshuffling. 
● Scenarios 2: Descending size-ordered splitting to expose ordering-induced scale bias.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The optimization signal is supervised training loss, while the headline outcome is established by objective ground-truth-based detection metrics on held-out test subsets, with no learned or automated evaluator reused across both roles.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard COCO-style detection metrics, primarily mAP@0.50:0.95, computed against ground-truth annotations on held-out test splits [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0038, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0040, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0047].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised bounding-box loss during YOLOv11n training on each partitioning scenario's training subset [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0005, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0036].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims are well aligned with the findings: the authors note that size-aware stratification substantially improves upon adversarial/size-ordered partitions while performing comparably to natural unsorted splits that already possess balanced scale distributions, explicitly avoiding overclaiming universal superiority over standard random splits [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0054, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0056, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0057].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is conducted under controlled conditions with fixed YOLOv11n detector hyperparameters, measuring detection performance using standard metrics (mAP@0.50:0.95, mAP@0.50, precision, recall, and F1) [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0036, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0047, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0048]. The results clearly illustrate how severe ordering/partitioning bias degrades detector evaluation and how stratification mitigates it [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0043, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0056].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard supervised object detection evaluation on held-out test subsets using established objective benchmarks does not exhibit circular evaluator reuse.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard COCO evaluation metrics (mAP@0.50:0.95) computed against ground-truth annotations on the held-out test splits [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0038, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0040, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0047].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised bounding box loss during YOLOv11n training on the training partition subsets [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0005, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0036].

primary.limitations: The authors transparently discuss the scope and limitations, noting that the study is conducted on two domain-specific license plate datasets and with a single detector architecture, leaving multi-class datasets and multiple architectures to future work [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0057, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0058].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly defined: it systematically compares four partitioning scenarios (natural sequential split, descending size-ordered split, stratified size-descending split, and size-aware stratified sampling) across two split directions, while tracking subset scale divergence using KL divergence and EMD [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0025, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0028, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0029, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0030, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0034].
primary.quality_rationale: The study addresses a sound data-centric question regarding the impact of dataset partitioning on object detection evaluation with clear experimental controls, appropriate baseline comparisons, and well-contextualized interpretations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper provides an empirical study examining how object-size distribution shifts introduced by dataset partitioning strategies affect the evaluation and training of object detectors (specifically YOLOv11n) on two license-plate datasets [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0004, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0005].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study addresses a sound data-centric question regarding the impact of dataset partitioning on object detection evaluation with clear experimental controls, appropriate baseline comparisons, and well-contextualized interpretations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently discuss the scope and limitations, noting that the study is conducted on two domain-specific license plate datasets and with a single detector architecture, leaving multi-class datasets and multiple architectures to future work [E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0057, E133b4a6fca0a7e81-B0058].
